rules.reason: This family differs mainly in how much certainty is built before the first real-world test.
The action-first variant creates evidence before doing broad comparison.
Hybrid gives one small clarity step and then moves to evidence quickly.

secondaryEvidence.use: Reinforces or weakens the startingMode ranking. Past success with planning favors Clarity-first; past success with experiments favors Action-first; mixed success favors Hybrid.

eligibilityOrVetoSignals.use: Does not meaningfully distinguish these three variants because weekly load is deliberately held similar. It decides whether this whole variant family is feasible or needs a lower-load family.
Mostly a veto/adaptation signal here. For example, 'too many things to do' may require a lower-density family rather than choosing among these three.
Held intentionally similar across the three variants, so it should not decide this comparison. A separate structured-vs-flexible variant family is needed to test this signal.
Held at balanced ambition across all three. It should select an ambition family, not decide among these starting-mode variants.

goalSpecificSignals.use: All three assume DIRECTION_EVIDENCE_GAP. If the Expert finds a different primary bottleneck, none of these variants should be selected.
All three contain one information conversation. If involving another person is a major blocker, the selected variant should be adapted or a solo family should exist.
